{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q001_histone_related_proteins","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, histones sit in class a, All alpha proteins, at fold a.22, Histone-fold. That fold contains a single curated superfamily, a.22.1, also named Histone-fold, so its curated member families are all SCOPe superfamily-level relatives of one another: a.22.1.1 Nucleosome core histones, a.22.1.2 Archaeal histone, a.22.1.3 TBP-associated factors, TAFs, and a.22.1.4 Bacterial histone-fold protein. Thus archaeal histones, bacterial histone-fold proteins, and histone-fold TAF subunits are the non-core-histone groups SCOPe places with nucleosome core histones at the same fold and superfamily. The family split is important: a TAF or bacterial histone-fold domain should not be annotated as a eukaryotic nucleosome core histone solely from the shared fold, nor should nucleosome DNA-packing function be transferred wholesale across families. The shared a.22.1 superfamily is evidence for a probable evolutionary relationship and for the conserved histone-fold core as a structural template, but template choice and functional transfer should stay family-aware; SCOPe also has a.22.1.0 automated matches under this superfamily, which are candidates rather than a named curated biological family.","evidence_used":["get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.22","get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.22/parents","list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.22/children?limit=100","list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.22.1/children?limit=100"]}]}
